label: Some animals arise by spontaneous generation from putrefying matter
claim: Some animals are born from parents of their own kind, while others arise spontaneously and not from kindred stock, some of them out of putrefying earth or vegetable matter (as many insects do) and others inside animals out of the secretions of their organs.
quote: some spring from parent animals according to their kind, whilst others grow spontaneously and not from kindred stock; and of these instances of spontaneous generation some come from putrefying earth or vegetable matter, as is the case with a number of insects
scope: animals generally, especially insects and internal parasites
measurable_quantities: whether any animal arises from putrefying matter without parents (sterile-medium exclusion experiments)
candidate_data: Classic exclusion experiments (Redi, Spallanzani, Pasteur) and life-cycle records for insects and parasites in the Animal Diversity Web.

label: Female cartilaginous fishes are larger than males
claim: In the cartilaginous fishes (selachians) the female is larger than the male, and the same holds for most other fishes.
quote: In the cartilaginous species the female is larger than the male; and the same is the case with other fishes for the most part.
scope: selachians (sharks, rays, skates) and fishes generally
measurable_quantities: female vs male maximum or mean body length by species
candidate_data: Sex-specific maximum lengths and length at maturity in FishBase.

label: Male sharks and dogfish have two appendages near the vent
claim: In cartilaginous fishes the male, unlike the female, has two appendages hanging down near the vent, and this sex difference is found in all species of sharks and dogfish.
quote: in cartilaginous fishes the male, in some species, differs from the female in the fact that he is furnished with two appendages hanging down from about the exit of the residuum, and that the female is not so furnished
measurable_quantities: presence of paired pelvic claspers in males and absence in females across shark species
candidate_data: Comparative anatomy of chondrichthyan claspers in Phenoscape and Uberon; species accounts in FishBase.

label: Fishes and footless animals lack testicles but have paired sperm ducts
claim: Neither fishes nor any footless animals have testicles; instead male serpents and male fishes have a pair of ducts that fill with milt in the breeding season and discharge a milky fluid.
quote: Now neither fishes nor any animals devoid of feet are furnished with testicles, but male serpents and male fishes have a pair of ducts which fill with milt or sperm at the rutting season
measurable_quantities: presence of testes in male fishes and snakes
candidate_data: Gonad anatomy in Uberon and Phenoscape; fish reproductive anatomy summaries in FishBase.

label: Birds and footed egg-layers have internal testicles
claim: Birds have their testicles inside the body, and so do all oviparous animals that have feet.
quote: birds, by the way, have their testicles in their interior, and so have all ovipara that are furnished with feet
measurable_quantities: position of testes (abdominal vs scrotal) across birds, reptiles and amphibians
candidate_data: Testis position in Uberon and Phenoscape; comparative anatomy literature.

label: Non-viviparous animals lack a bladder, except the tortoise
claim: Animals that are not viviparous have no bladder, with the single exception of the tortoise.
quote: these animals are unprovided with a bladder except in the case of the tortoise
measurable_quantities: presence of a urinary bladder across birds, lizards, snakes, turtles, amphibians and fishes
candidate_data: Urinary bladder presence across taxa in Uberon and Phenoscape.

label: A female partridge downwind of the male becomes impregnated
claim: A female partridge becomes impregnated if she gets to leeward of the male, and often merely by hearing his voice or by his breathing on her as he flies overhead.
quote: With partridges, by the way, if the female gets to leeward of the male, she becomes thereby impregnated.
measurable_quantities: fertility of eggs from female partridges isolated from physical contact with males
candidate_data: Poultry and gamebird reproductive physiology literature on fertilization requiring copulation.

label: Cephalopods copulate mouth to mouth by interlacing tentacles
claim: The octopus, the cuttlefish and the squid all mate in the same way, uniting at the mouth by interlacing their tentacles.
quote: Molluscs, such as the octopus, the sepia, and the calamary, have sexual intercourse all in the same way; that is to say, they unite at the mouth, by an interlacing of their tentacles.
measurable_quantities: mating positions recorded for octopus, cuttlefish and squid species
candidate_data: Behavioural observations of cephalopod mating in the literature and species accounts in SeaLifeBase.

label: In insects the female inserts her organ into the male
claim: In copulating insects the female pushes her sexual organ up into the body of the male, the reverse of what happens in other animals.
quote: The female pushes from underneath her sexual organ into the body of the male above, this being the reverse of the operation observed in other creatures
scope: insects, e.g. flies and cantharid beetles
measurable_quantities: direction of genital intromission in insect copulation
candidate_data: Insect genital morphology and copulation studies in the entomological literature.

label: Most animals mate in spring, when winter turns to summer
claim: Animals in general are naturally disposed to mate at about the same time of year, in spring as winter changes into summer, when almost all flying, walking and swimming creatures pair.
quote: Animals in general seem naturally disposed to this intercourse at about the same period of the year, and that is when winter is changing into summer.
measurable_quantities: breeding or mating month by species across taxa
candidate_data: Breeding-season fields in the Amniote Life-History Database, AnAge and FishBase spawning records.

label: The halcyon breeds at the winter solstice
claim: The halcyon (kingfisher) breeds at the time of the winter solstice, unlike nearly all other birds, which breed in spring and early summer.
quote: The halcyon breeds at the season of the winter solstice.
scope: the halcyon (usually identified as the common kingfisher)
measurable_quantities: breeding month of the common kingfisher in the Mediterranean
candidate_data: Breeding phenology of Alcedo atthis in nest-record schemes and the Animal Diversity Web.

label: Most wild animals give birth only once a year
claim: Most wild animals bring forth young once and only once a year, except animals such as the hare whose females can conceive again while already pregnant.
quote: The greater part of wild animals bring forth once and once only in the year, except in the case of animals like the hare, where the female can become superfoetally impregnated.
measurable_quantities: litters or clutches per year by species
occurrence of superfetation in hares
candidate_data: Litters per year in PanTHERIA and the Amniote Life-History Database; superfetation studies in the European brown hare.

label: The pelamys and the tunny breed only in the Black Sea
claim: The pelamys (young tunny or bonito) and the tunny breed in the Black Sea and nowhere else.
quote: The pelamys and the tunny breed in the Euxine, and nowhere else.
scope: tunny (Atlantic bluefin tuna) and pelamys (bonito or young tunny)
measurable_quantities: locations of spawning grounds of bluefin tuna and Atlantic bonito
candidate_data: Spawning-ground records in FishBase and ICCAT bluefin tuna assessments; larval occurrences in GBIF and OBIS.

label: The brooding female octopus stops feeding and loses condition
claim: The female octopus, after laying her eggs, broods over them and loses condition because she does not go out for food during the hatching period.
quote: The female, after laying her eggs, broods over them, and in consequence gets out of condition, by reason of not going in quest of food during the hatching period.
measurable_quantities: feeding rate and body mass of brooding female octopuses
candidate_data: Studies of maternal brooding and post-spawning senescence in Octopus vulgaris; SeaLifeBase species accounts.

label: Sea urchins have most eggs in warm weather and at full moon
claim: The edible sea urchin is never without its so-called eggs, but has them in greatest abundance in spring and autumn, in warm weather, and when the moon is full.
quote: it is furnished with them in especial abundance in warm weather or when a full moon is in the sky
scope: edible sea urchin (probably Paracentrotus lividus); excluding urchins of the Pyrrhaean Straits
measurable_quantities: gonad index of sea urchins by season and lunar phase
candidate_data: Published gonad-index time series for Mediterranean sea urchins and studies of lunar spawning periodicity.

label: Wild birds breed once a year; the swallow and blackbird twice
claim: Wild birds as a rule pair and breed only once a year, but the swallow and the blackbird breed twice.
quote: Of birds the wild species, as has been stated, as a general rule pair and breed only once a year. The swallow, however, and the blackbird breed twice.
measurable_quantities: broods per year by bird species
candidate_data: Broods-per-year fields in the Amniote Life-History Database and national nest-record schemes.

label: Ring-dove is the largest pigeon, the turtle-dove the smallest
claim: Among the pigeons the ring-dove is the largest, the stock-dove next and a little larger than the common pigeon, and the turtle-dove the smallest.
quote: The largest of all the pigeon species is the phatta or ring-dove; and the next in size is the oenas or stock-dove; and the stock-dove is a little larger than the common pigeon. The smallest of all the species is the turtle-dove.
scope: Greek columbids: wood pigeon, stock dove, rock/domestic pigeon, turtle dove
measurable_quantities: body mass and wing length of Columba palumbus, C. oenas, C. livia and Streptopelia turtur
candidate_data: Body mass and morphometrics in AVONET and the Amniote Life-History Database.

label: The first semen produced is infertile or yields poor offspring
claim: In all animals the earliest semen produced is infertile, or if fertile gives smaller and poorer offspring, as seen especially in man, viviparous quadrupeds and birds (whose first eggs are smaller).
quote: in all animals, the earliest secretion of sperm is unfruitful, or if it be fruitful the issue is comparatively poor and small
scope: copulating animals, especially man, viviparous quadrupeds and birds
measurable_quantities: fertility and offspring size by parental age at first reproduction
egg size of first clutches vs later clutches
candidate_data: Livestock and poultry breeding records on young-sire fertility and pullet egg size; human andrology studies of adolescent semen.

label: Men produce semen at about fourteen and are fertile at about twenty-one
claim: A man begins to produce seminal fluid at about fourteen years of age and becomes capable of generation at about twenty-one.
quote: Man begins to possess seminal fluid about the age of fourteen, and becomes generatively capable at about the age of twenty-one years.
measurable_quantities: age at spermarche
age at which male fertility is established
candidate_data: Human pubertal development and spermarche studies in the clinical literature.

label: Females and young animals have higher-pitched voices than males and adults
claim: As a general rule the female has a higher-pitched voice than the male, and the young animal than the older one.
quote: As a general rule the female is sharper-toned in voice than the male, and the young animal than the elder
scope: vocal animals, e.g. deer, dogs, horses, humans
measurable_quantities: fundamental frequency of calls by sex and age
candidate_data: Bioacoustic recordings in the Macaulay Library and xeno-canto, and published studies of vocal pitch by sex and age.

label: In cattle the cow's voice is deeper than the bull's
claim: In cattle, contrary to the general rule, the cow has a deeper voice than the bull, and calves a deeper voice than grown cattle.
quote: the cow has a deeper note than the bull, and the calves a deeper note than the cattle
measurable_quantities: fundamental frequency of vocalizations of cows, bulls and calves
candidate_data: Bioacoustic studies of cattle vocalizations by sex and age.

label: Castrated males take on female characters, including voice
claim: Male animals that are castrated take on the characters of the female, which explains the change of voice in gelded animals.
quote: And we can thus understand the change of voice in animals that undergo gelding; for male animals that undergo this process assume the characters of the female.
measurable_quantities: voice pitch and secondary sexual characters in castrated vs intact males
candidate_data: Veterinary and endocrinological studies of castration effects in livestock.

label: The bitch's gestation lasts sixty to sixty-three days
claim: Gestation in the dog lasts sixty to sixty-three days and never less than sixty, or if less the litter does not survive.
quote: The period of gestation with the bitch is sixty days, or sixty-one, or sixty-two, or sixty-three at the utmost
measurable_quantities: gestation length in dogs (days)
candidate_data: Gestation length for Canis familiaris in AnAge, PanTHERIA and veterinary breeding records.

label: Stallions live about thirty-five years, mares a little over forty
claim: The stallion as a rule lives about thirty-five years and the mare a little over forty, so that horses remain sexually capable almost all their lives.
quote: the stallion, as a rule, lives for about thirty-five years, and the mare for a little over forty
measurable_quantities: typical and maximum lifespan of horses by sex
candidate_data: Maximum and typical longevity of Equus caballus in AnAge and equine demographic studies.

label: Men are generative to about sixty-five, women conceive to about forty-five
claim: As a rule a man can beget children up to about sixty-five and a woman can conceive up to about forty-five; at most the limits are seventy and fifty, and these are rare.
quote: As a rule, the male is generative up to the age of sixty-five, and to the age of forty-five the female is capable of conception.
measurable_quantities: age at last birth for women
paternal age distribution at oldest paternity
candidate_data: Natural-fertility demographic data (e.g. Hutterite records) and menopause-age studies.

label: Camel gestation lasts twelve months with a single young
claim: The camel carries its young for twelve months and never bears more than one at a time.
quote: Its period of gestation is twelve months; and it is never delivered of more than one foal at a time.
measurable_quantities: gestation length and litter size in Camelus dromedarius
candidate_data: Gestation length and litter size in AnAge and PanTHERIA.

label: Elephant gestation lasts two years with a single calf
claim: The female elephant carries her young for two years and bears only one at a time.
quote: The period of gestation with the female is two years; and only one young animal is produced at a time, in other words it is uniparous.
measurable_quantities: gestation length and litter size in elephants
candidate_data: Gestation length and litter size for Elephas maximus and Loxodonta africana in AnAge and PanTHERIA.

label: All testaceans are spontaneously generated in mud, according to the material
claim: As a general rule all testaceans (shelled molluscs and the like) arise by spontaneous generation in mud, and differ according to the material: oysters in slime, cockles on sandy bottoms, ascidians, barnacles and limpets in rock hollows.
quote: As a general rule, then, all testaceans grow by spontaneous generation in mud, differing from one another according to the differences of the material
scope: testaceans: oysters, cockles, mussels, scallops, limpets, ascidians, barnacles
measurable_quantities: presence of spawning, larvae and parental origin in bivalves, gastropods, barnacles and ascidians
candidate_data: Life-cycle and larval-stage records for marine invertebrates in SeaLifeBase and the Animal Diversity Web.

label: The murex lives about six years, with yearly growth marked on its shell
claim: The purple murex lives about six years, and each year's growth is marked by a distinct interval in the spiral of its shell.
quote: The murex lives for about six years; and the yearly increase is indicated by a distinct interval in the spiral convolution of the shell.
measurable_quantities: lifespan of murex snails
periodicity of shell growth marks (annual or not)
candidate_data: Sclerochronology and age-growth studies of Mediterranean murex species; SeaLifeBase life-history fields.

label: The pinna dies if deprived of its pinna-guard crab or shrimp
claim: The pinna (fan mussel) houses a small shrimp or crab, the pinna-guard, and if it loses this companion it soon dies.
quote: these creatures have inside them a parasite nicknamed the pinna-guard, in some cases a small carid and in other cases a little crab; if the pinna be deprived of this pinna-guard it soon dies
scope: Pinna nobilis and its commensal shrimps and pea crabs
measurable_quantities: survival of fan mussels with and without commensal decapods
candidate_data: Studies of Pinna nobilis symbionts (Pontonia, Nepinnotheres); SeaLifeBase.

label: Eggs of crustaceans, molluscs and oviparous fishes grow after laying
claim: In crustaceans, molluscs and oviparous fishes the egg continues to grow after it has been laid.
quote: This same phenomenon is observable in molluscs also, and in such fishes as are oviparous; for in all these cases the egg continues to grow.
measurable_quantities: egg diameter or volume over incubation
candidate_data: Egg-size change during incubation in crustacean, cephalopod and fish embryology studies.

label: Squid, cuttlefish and octopus rarely live beyond a year
claim: The squid and the cuttlefish are short-lived and with few exceptions do not live out a year, and the same is true of the octopus.
quote: The calamary and the cuttle-fish are short-lived, as, with few exceptions, they never see the year out; and the same statement is applicable to the octopus.
measurable_quantities: lifespan of Loligo, Sepia and Octopus species
candidate_data: Cephalopod age (statolith) studies and lifespan records in AnAge and SeaLifeBase.

label: The whole insect grub develops into the animal, not part of it
claim: All insects produce grubs (except one kind of butterfly that lays a hard egg), and the young insect develops from the whole grub, not from a part of it as an animal develops from part of an egg.
quote: But from the grub, the young animal does not grow out of a mere portion of it, as a young animal grows from a portion only of an egg, but the grub entire grows and the animal becomes differentiated out of it.
measurable_quantities: whether insect larvae are wholly transformed into the adult or contain a separate yolk-fed embryo
candidate_data: Insect developmental biology on metamorphosis and egg stages.

label: Intestinal worms do not reproduce their kind
claim: Intestinal worms, of which there are three kinds (flat-worm, round-worm and ascarid), never propagate their kind, although the flat-worm lays something like a melon seed.
quote: These intestinal worms do not in any case propagate their kind.
scope: intestinal worms of man: tapeworm, roundworm, pinworm
measurable_quantities: egg production and life cycles of Taenia, Ascaris and Enterobius
candidate_data: Parasite life-cycle data from CDC DPDx and parasitology literature.

label: Caterpillars feed and excrete; chrysalises do neither
claim: The butterfly caterpillar feeds and voids excrement, but once it becomes a chrysalis it neither feeds nor voids excrement; the same holds for all insects that develop from a grub, such as bees and wasps.
quote: At first, when it is a caterpillar, it feeds and ejects excrement; but when it turns into the chrysalis it neither feeds nor ejects excrement.
measurable_quantities: feeding and excretion during larval vs pupal stages
candidate_data: Insect physiology of the pupal stage; species accounts in the Animal Diversity Web.

label: Generation of grubs is due primarily to the sun's heat or wind
claim: In all grubs and all animals that emerge from the grub state, generation is caused primarily by the heat of the sun or by wind.
quote: With all grubs and all animals that break out from the grub state, generation is due primarily to the heat of the sun or to wind.
measurable_quantities: dependence of insect emergence on temperature
whether larvae arise without eggs
candidate_data: Insect phenology and degree-day development models; spontaneous-generation exclusion experiments.

label: A winged animal in Cyprus is generated in copper-smelting fires
claim: In Cyprus, where copper ore is smelted, a winged animal somewhat larger than a bluebottle fly is generated in the fire, can hop or crawl through it, and perishes when kept away from the fire.
quote: In Cyprus, in places where copper-ore is smelted, with heaps of the ore piled on day after day, an animal is engendered in the fire, somewhat larger than a blue bottle fly, furnished with wings, which can hop or crawl through the fire.
scope: an unnamed insect of Cypriot copper smelters
measurable_quantities: survival of any insect in smelting fires
candidate_data: Upper thermal limits of insects in thermal-tolerance compilations such as GlobTherm.

label: Ichneumon wasps provision mud-sealed holes with dead spiders
claim: The wasps called ichneumons, smaller than ordinary wasps, kill spiders, carry them to a hole in a wall, seal it with mud and lay their grubs inside, and from the grubs come new ichneumons.
quote: kill spiders and carry off the dead bodies to a wall or some such place with a hole in it; this hole they smear over with mud and lay their grubs inside it, and from the grubs come the hunter-wasps
measurable_quantities: prey type and nest construction of spider-hunting wasps
candidate_data: Nesting-biology accounts for Pompilidae and Sceliphron in the entomological literature and the Animal Diversity Web.

label: Bees make wax from flowers but gather honey from the air
claim: The bee makes wax from flowers but does not make honey; it merely gathers honey that is deposited out of the atmosphere as dew.
quote: The bee, then, makes the wax from flowers. The honey, however, it does not make, but merely gathers what is deposited out of the atmosphere
measurable_quantities: origin of honey sugars (floral nectar or honeydew vs atmospheric dew)
glandular origin of wax
candidate_data: Apicultural physiology on nectar processing and wax glands; melissopalynology of honey.

label: A bee lives six years, at most seven
claim: The bee lives six years as a rule and seven at most.
quote: The bee lives for six years as a rule, as an exception for seven years.
measurable_quantities: lifespan of worker and queen honey bees
colony longevity
candidate_data: Honey bee longevity records in AnAge and apicultural literature.

label: Young scorpions and spiders kill their parent after hatching
claim: When the land-scorpion's brood has hatched, the young eject and kill the parent, as also happens with the spider.
quote: When the hatching is completed, the parent animal, as happens with the parent spider, is ejected and put to death by the young ones
measurable_quantities: incidence of matriphagy in scorpions and spiders
candidate_data: Arachnological studies of matriphagy and maternal care.

label: Grasshoppers lay eggs at summer's end and then die
claim: The grasshopper lays its eggs at the close of summer and dies after laying them, the males dying about the same time.
quote: The grasshopper lays its eggs at the close of summer, and dies after laying them.
measurable_quantities: adult lifespan after oviposition and oviposition season in grasshoppers
candidate_data: Life-history records for Orthoptera in the Orthoptera Species File and entomological literature.

label: Only male cicadas sing
claim: In both the large and small cicadas it is the male that sings and the female is silent.
quote: In both species, the larger and the smaller, it is the male that sings, and the female that is unvocal.
measurable_quantities: presence of tymbal sound organs by sex in cicadas
candidate_data: Cicada acoustic anatomy and bioacoustic recordings in the entomological literature.

label: Lice, fleas and bugs produce nits that generate nothing
claim: Insects that live on the juices of living flesh, such as lice, fleas and bugs, all produce nits, and these nits produce nothing further.
quote: all, without exception, generate what are called 'nits', and these nits generate nothing
measurable_quantities: hatching of louse, flea and bedbug eggs into nymphs or larvae
candidate_data: Life cycles of Pediculus, Pulex and Cimex in medical entomology references such as CDC DPDx.

label: The ass alone among hairy animals has neither lice nor ticks
claim: All feathered and hair-coated animals are infested with lice, with the single exception of the ass, which has neither lice nor ticks.
quote: All other winged animals that are furnished with feathers are similarly infested, and all hair-coated creatures also, with the single exception of the ass, which is infested neither with lice nor with ticks.
measurable_quantities: records of lice and ticks on donkeys
louse presence across bird and mammal hosts
candidate_data: Host-parasite association records for Haematopinus asini and ticks on Equus asinus in veterinary parasitology databases.

label: Fig-wasps from wild figs enter cultivated figs and keep them from dropping
claim: The fig-wasp develops in the fruit of the wild fig, then flies into the fruit of the cultivated fig through its opening and makes the fruit stay on the tree, which is why farmers hang wild figs on fig trees.
quote: the psen leaves the husk behind it and flies away, and enters into the fruit of the fig-tree through its orifice, and causes the fruit not to drop off
scope: fig wasp (Blastophaga psenes) and Ficus carica (caprification)
measurable_quantities: fruit retention of caprified vs uncaprified figs
candidate_data: Horticultural studies of caprification in Smyrna-type figs and fig-wasp pollination ecology.

label: The viper is internally oviparous and externally viviparous
claim: The viper produces eggs internally but gives birth to live young, all in one day, about twenty in number and one at a time, whereas other serpents lay eggs.
quote: the viper is externally viviparous, having been previously oviparous internally
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode and litter size of Vipera species
candidate_data: Reproductive mode and clutch or litter size in the Reptile Database and the Amniote Life-History Database.
